It can also argue at the locating stage that a place merely passed through is not where in substance the tort arose.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C3.6.1 :: Threshold

Per Rickshaw, courts "must not be quick" to apply it unless [the displaced law] is purely fortuitous and applying it causes [injustice], on "clear and satisfying grounds" (Lord Wilberforce), lest it become [a proper law of the tort].

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
  1. 1
    What changes: the place of the act is unknown

    Back to the base facts with one change: the engineer wrote and sent the update from a laptop on a train that crossed Elbonia, Suburbia and Ruritania, and the logs do not show where the train was. Norvik still pleads Elbonia and Elbonian law, and no one pleads Suburbian law. The conspiracy claim and the locating rule stay as they were; only the place of the careless act is now unknown.

  2. 2
    The gap in the evidence hurts Norvik K6

    Per EFT Holdings, limb 2 exists for the defendant's benefit, so Norvik must plead and prove that the law it relies on gives no liability. The same should follow for showing that Elbonian law is engaged at all, and Norvik cannot place the act in Elbonia. A party that pleads foreign law and fails to prove its case under it may simply lose (Brownlie; EFT Holdings), and in Rickshaw an unevidenced place of receipt was “speculative”, so Singapore law applied. With the act unplaced, every other route gives liability: Ruritania, where the damage was done, makes Norvik liable, and Suburbian law is not pleaded, so Singapore law would apply by default. Norvik will reply that Elbonia, its base, is still the place in substance, so its limb 2 defence probably, not certainly, fails. No foreign rule on proof is in play, and a proper law of the tort (a closest-connection test) was rejected (Red Sea).

  3. 3
    If the train was in Suburbia N5

    Suppose the logs show Suburbia and Norvik proves that Suburbian law gives no claim. Xanthe argues first, at the locating stage, that a place merely passed through is not where in substance the tort arose. If that fails, it invokes the exception: a country crossed on a train is purely fortuitous, like a transit lounge, so Suburbian law is displaced and Singapore law alone remains, under which Norvik is liable. The presumption of similarity cannot be used once Suburbian law is proved to differ.

5Scorecards: weigh the factors

Prof Chong rewards applying facts to factor tests. Sort each fact, then answer the verdict question. These use the base facts unless a line says “Suppose”.

N3 Sort the factors: Locating the conspiracy on the base facts

Ibis and Mr Thorne say the conspiracy was committed in Suburbia. How much does each line count in finding the one place where the conspiracy in substance arose?

Ibis is incorporated and based in Utopia.
Real weight. The identity and location of the conspirators is the first factor on the list. This one points to Utopia. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
Mr Thorne lives and works in Elbonia.
Real weight. Also the location of a conspirator. It points to Elbonia, so the conspirators' homes are split between two countries. Neither is Suburbia. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
The two met and made their agreement at a trade fair in Suburbia.
Little weight. Where they combined is on the list, so it counts for something. But it is one factor, not the test, and a trade fair that neither lives near is close to an accident. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
Mr Thorne slowed the servers from his desk in Elbonia.
Real weight. A concerted act done in pursuance of the agreement. It points to Elbonia. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
Ibis ran its adverts in Utopia in the same week.
Real weight. The other concerted act. It points to Utopia. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
Most of the players who left Xanthe were in Utopia.
Real weight. Where the losses arose is on the list. The custom was lost in Utopia. C3.3.2 :: Conspiracy
Xanthe books all its revenue in Singapore.
Little weight. The claimant's location is on the list, so it is not nothing. But it is the only link with Singapore, and loss recorded at the claimant's home base may be quite fortuitous. It does not by itself locate a tort. C3.3.1 :: Damage Not Determinative
Suburbian law has no tort of conspiracy.
Not a locating factor. What a law says does not help to locate the tort. Locate first, then ask what the law of that place provides. C3.3.1 :: §
Taking the payment was a crime under Elbonian law.
Not a locating factor. Criminality is not on the list. The test looks at where the elements of the tort occurred, as the lex fori recognises them. C3.3.1 :: The Test
⚡ Scorecard 1 · the verdictN3
Where was the conspiracy most likely committed, and what follows?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

One conspirator, one concerted act and the lost custom point to Utopia. The other conspirator and the other act point to Elbonia. Suburbia has only the meeting. Since conspiracy is a tort in both Utopia and Elbonia, the choice between them does not change the result.

🔎 More depth (Gemini's note, checked)

On the EFT Holdings list: the conspirators are in Utopia (Ibis) and Elbonia (Mr Thorne); the concerted acts were the slowing from Elbonia and the adverts in Utopia; the players were lost in Utopia; the agreement was made at a trade fair in Suburbia, which neither lives near; and Xanthe books its revenue in Singapore, which carries little weight. Utopia has the most, Elbonia next, and Suburbia only the meeting. Because both Utopian and Elbonian law treat conspiracy as a tort, limb 2 is met without choosing between them. What Suburbian law says, and Mr Thorne's crime under Elbonian law, play no part in locating the tort.

N5 Sort the factors: The flexible exception on the Twist 2 facts

In Twist 2 both companies are based in Singapore, and Xanthe wants to displace Elbonian law so that it can recover lost profits. Does each line help Xanthe, help Norvik, or carry no weight? Lines marked “Suppose” are extra facts for this card only.

Xanthe and Norvik are both incorporated and based in Singapore.
Helps Xanthe: displace Elbonian law. The parties' residence points away from Elbonia, as it did for the British servicemen in Boys v Chaplin. C3.6.1 :: Factors to Weigh
The engineer was on a six month posting in Elbonia and worked there every day.
Helps Norvik: keep it. This is not transit. Even soldiers stationed in Malta are less transient than passengers passing through, so Norvik says Elbonia is the natural place of the tort. C3.6.3 :: Rickshaw Caveat
The data that was destroyed sat on servers in Ruritania, not in Elbonia.
Helps Xanthe: displace Elbonian law. The place of injury is a factor, and it is not Elbonia. That weakens Elbonia's tie to the claim. C3.6.1 :: Factors to Weigh
Only the head of damage is in dispute. Both laws make Norvik liable.
Helps Xanthe: displace Elbonian law. Displacement may cover heads of damage only. Elbonia has little interest in limiting damages between two Singapore companies. C3.6.3 :: Issue-by-Issue
Singapore law would give Xanthe more money.
No weight. The exception is strictly applied. A party needs clear fortuity, not a more favourable law. C3.6.1 :: Strictly Applied
Xanthe chose to sue in Singapore.
No weight. The claimant's choice of forum is not a connecting factor. The court weighs the places of injury and conduct, the parties' residence and the centre of their relationship. C3.6.1 :: Factors to Weigh
Suppose: the engineer had sent the update from an Elbonian airport lounge while changing planes.
Helps Xanthe: displace Elbonian law. Transit is the clearest case of a purely fortuitous place. C3.6.1 :: Threshold
Suppose: Norvik had a permanent branch in Elbonia, and its whole update team worked there.
Helps Norvik: keep it. Elbonia would then be where the defendant carries on the very work complained of. Nothing about it would be accidental. C3.6.1 :: Threshold
⚡ Scorecard 2 · the verdictN5
What is the best conclusion on the Twist 2 facts?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

The shared Singapore home and the issue specific argument from Boys v Chaplin favour Xanthe. Rickshaw's strict fortuity test and the six month posting favour Norvik. State both, give the result under each, and then take a side. The exception works claim by claim and issue by issue, so it never carries over to the conspiracy claim.

🔎 More depth (Gemini's note, checked)

For Xanthe: both companies are based in Singapore, the data sat in Ruritania, only a head of loss is in dispute, and per Boys v Chaplin the law of the place of the tort may yield on damages alone where it has no interest in the parties. For Norvik: per Rickshaw the exception is strictly applied and needs a purely fortuitous place, and per C&Y even soldiers stationed in Malta are less transient than transit passengers, as is an engineer on a six-month posting. A more generous Singapore law and Xanthe's choice of forum count for nothing. Whatever the answer, the exception works claim by claim and issue by issue, so it does not touch the conspiracy claim.

6Remember

🧠 FOR THE EXAM
  • Run double actionability once per tort claim, and locate each tort by its own rule: the careless act for negligence, the EFT Holdings list for conspiracy.
  • Limb 1 is counterfactual and needs no link with Singapore; loss booked at the claimant's home base does not by itself locate a tort.
  • Where every candidate place gives the same result under limb 2, say so in a line and move on.
  • The exception needs a purely fortuitous place, not a kinder law; public policy is no ground for it, and it works claim by claim and issue by issue.
  • Online defamation is a separate tort wherever it is read; heads of loss are substance, while quantum and a final remedy such as a take down order are open points.
  • Limb 2 is the defendant's to plead and prove, so a gap in the evidence about where it acted hurts the defendant: its limb 2 defence probably fails.

LAW302 · META GAME · QUESTION 2 · HYPO q2-03 · GEMINI PROMPT V1 · 19 QUESTIONS

Perrin v Granit; Mr Halim v Perrin

Written by Claude for the drill and law reviewed. Gemini (prompt v1) wrote a guide to it; the guide was checked (1 corrections) and feeds the walkthrough. Gemini's file: law302_question_2_review_plain_english_study_gui.

Answers:

1Base facts

🧩 HYPOTHETICAL
Perrin v Granit; Mr Halim v Perrin

Perrin Plant Pte Ltd, a Singapore incorporated company, rebuilds used excavators at its yard in Singapore. Granit SA is a road builder incorporated in Ruritania. The Ruritanian state owns 60% of it.

In 2024 Perrin engaged Mr Halim, who lives in Ruritania, to use his family ties with Granit's state-appointed directors, in Ruritania, to win an order for Perrin. His commission of US$300,000 was payable in Ruritania once Granit signed. The engagement letter was signed in Singapore and has no governing law clause. No bribe is alleged.

On 10 January 2025 Granit signed a Supply Contract with Perrin for 40 excavators in four shipments, at US$1 million a shipment. It provides:

“5. Delivery: at the Buyer's depot at Port Ruri, Ruritania.”
“14. This contract is governed by Utopian law.”

Granit paid a deposit of US$500,000. Perrin delivered two shipments, and Granit has not paid for them. On 1 April 2025 Ruritania made it a crime to import excavators more than five years old. All Perrin's machines are older, so it sent nothing more. Granit asked for delivery at Port Arca in Arcadia, the nearest port outside Ruritania. Perrin refused.

Perrin sues Granit in the General Division for US$2 million. Granit pleads illegality. It counterclaims damages of US$900,000 for the two missing shipments and the return of its deposit. Mr Halim sues Perrin for his commission. Assume that the court has jurisdiction.

Advise Perrin on all the claims.

ℹ ASSUME
  1. Singapore has friendly relations with Ruritania, Utopia and Arcadia.
  2. Under Ruritanian law a contract to pay for influence over a state-owned company is against public policy and void. It is not a crime. Singapore public policy also condemns such contracts.
  3. Under Utopian law, a seller who cannot lawfully deliver at the agreed place must deliver at the nearest lawful port if the buyer asks. Under Singapore law, assume that the contract would be frustrated.
  4. Under Utopian law, Mr Halim's engagement is closely enough connected to the Supply Contract to bar Perrin's claim on it. Under Singapore law and Ruritanian law it is not.
  5. Nothing in Utopian law makes the Supply Contract unlawful.
✔ ROUND 1 · WHICH MENU BOXES?Note the boxes you would tick, then tap to compare.

Write from these boxes

  • M1
    Illegality: pick the route. Granit pleads illegality, and three countries' rules are in play. Label the proper law, the forum and the place of performance for each contract first, then pick a route for each rule.
  • M2
    The law broken is the proper law itself. Ask first whether the law broken is the proper law itself. For the Supply Contract it is not: Utopian law governs and the ban is Ruritanian. For the engagement letter it may be, if its objective proper law is Ruritanian.
  • M5
    Ralli Bros: performance becomes illegal where it must be done. A ban passed after signing makes unlawful the very delivery that clause 5 requires in Ruritania. That is Ralli, and the Utopian rule on delivery at the nearest lawful port makes the three readings give different results.
  • L6
    SCORECARD · Objective proper law: closest and most real connection. The engagement letter has no governing law clause. Its proper law must be weighed, not just named: signing and Perrin in Singapore, Mr Halim's work and his commission in Ruritania.
  • M4
    Lemenda: against the public policy of the place of performance. A commission for using influence, against public policy where the influence is used, with no statute broken. That is Lemenda, which needs Singapore to share the policy.
  • M6
    SCORECARD · Tainting: a relevant illegality, sufficiently connected. Granit says that the engagement taints the Supply Contract. The facts give a sufficient connection under one law and not under another, which is step 2 of tainting.
  • M7
    Repugnant contracts; illegality used as a defence. Granit wants its deposit back, and Perrin will point to the Supply Contract to keep it. One line on relying on a contract touched by illegality as a defence.

Decoys: tempting, but wrong on these facts

  • M3
    SCORECARD · Foster v Driscoll: intention to break a friendly state's law. Tempting because importing the machines is now a crime in a friendly state. Wrong because Foster turns on an intention, at signing, to break a foreign law. The ban came after signing, so no one had that intention.
  • K8
    Forum public policy; renvoi. Tempting because Singapore public policy also condemns buying influence. Wrong because that is a domestic policy, which works only together with the policy of the place of performance under Lemenda. Fundamental public policy is narrower.
  • L4
    Law chosen to dodge another country's rule. Tempting because Utopian law has no link with the deal. Wrong because a chosen law needs no connection, and nothing suggests that it was chosen to dodge a rule. The ban did not exist at signing.
  • L9
    Other attacks on the clause; capacity. Tempting because a state-owned buyer suggests a capacity point. Wrong because nothing says that Granit lacked power to buy excavators.
  • K3
    Damages: head or quantum. Tempting because a figure for damages is claimed. Wrong because no law is said to deny or cap that head of loss. The fight is over illegality, not over the measure of damages.

Fair to tick but not needed: L1 Starter: the proper law and its three stages, L2 Express choice of law clause, L5 No clause: implied choice, K1 Characterise the issue

Application questions · base facts

⚡ Base facts · 1 of 7M1
Before any illegality rule is applied to the Supply Contract, which laws can matter?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Only three kinds of law can matter: the proper law, the lex fori and the law of the place of performance. Illegality at the place of contracting, or at a party's residence or place of incorporation, is irrelevant (Sim See Kee). Ruritania counts because clause 5 requires delivery there, not because Granit is Ruritanian.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.1 :: Irrelevant Laws

Per Sim See Kee (and Kleinwort), illegality at [the place of contracting / a party's residence or incorporation] is irrelevant; conversely, per Dimskal, legality at [the LLS] cannot save [a contract illegal under the proper law / a forum mandatory rule / forum international policy].

⚡ Base facts · 2 of 7M5
Granit counterclaims for the two missing shipments. Perrin pleads the import ban. What decides the point?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Ralli looks to the act the contract requires at the contractual place of performance. Its basis has three readings and here they differ. Start with the independent rule (Esben), then run frustration under the proper law, where Utopian law keeps the contract alive. Granit can add that, even on the first reading, a lawful port under the proper law means no unlawful act is demanded in Ruritania. Singapore's frustration rule is irrelevant because Singapore law is only the lex fori.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.5 :: Basis: Three Readings (results differ, so run them)

Per C&Y (and Day), Ralli is (1) an independent conflicts rule, (2) frustration under [the proper law], or (3) comity-based abstention, and [the result] turns on [the reading].

  • (1) Independent rule (start here): per Esben, Dicey's rule rooted in comity, catching [supervening] and initial illegality alike, and per Prof Chong arguably preferable as [the later, more unequivocal] SGCA ruling.
  • (2) Frustration (alternative): Peh Teck Quee leaned to it, declining Ralli where [the ban pre-dated the contract], so ask whether [the proper law] frustrates or permits [delivery elsewhere].
  • (3) Comity abstention: supported by dicta (Toprak; Magdeev), but per Peh Teck Quee Ralli has "nothing to do with" [public policy], unlike [Foster].
  • When it matters: per Ryder Industries, only where [the proper law] is not [the lex fori], as Singapore domestic law frustrates [the contract] anyway.
  • Haze twist: per Chong (seminar), if [Indonesia bans gas exports], reading (1) refuses enforcement against [the Indonesian supplier], an odd result for [the Singapore buyer], whereas under (2) [the proper law] decides whether [the contract] is frustrated.
⚡ Base facts · 3 of 7M5
Does the ban also excuse Granit from paying for the two shipments already delivered?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Ralli makes a contract unenforceable “in so far as” performance is unlawful at the contractual place of performance. The price claim does not ask the court to enforce an unlawful act. The penal law answer is wrong because a foreign penal law is recognised as a fact, not enforced.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.5 :: Illegal Performance

Per Ralli Brothers, [freight above the decreed rate in Barcelona / delivery into X after its ban] is unenforceable in so far as unlawful at [the contractual place of performance], whatever [the proper law].

⚡ Base facts · 4 of 7M4
Mr Halim sues for his commission. How should the answer deal with his claim?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

No written law is broken, so this is not Foster. Run the proper law first. The place where both parties perform is Ruritania, which points to Ruritanian law, under which the contract is void. If Singapore law governs, Lemenda is met squarely: the forum's policy and the policy of the place of performance coincide. The debate about a third proper law that does not condemn the contract does not arise.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.4 :: Double Policy Breach

Per Lemenda, [a commission for influencing Qatari officials] under [an English-law contract] is unenforced if contrary to both a forum policy founded on general morality and the same policy at [the place where influence is to be exerted].

  • Domestic tier: per Phillips J, [buying influence] offends only domestic forum policy (it bites if [performed here]), hence the LLS element; international policy would make [the LLS / proper law] immaterial.
⚡ Base facts · 5 of 7M6
Perrin plans to defeat Mr Halim's claim by arguing that the engagement is unenforceable. What is the risk in that?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Step 1 of tainting asks whether Singapore would enforce the related contract. If Perrin itself shows that it would not, it has made that part of Granit's case. Whether a breach of public policy alone is serious enough to taint is unclear, so Perrin cannot rely on the threshold to protect it.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.6 :: Starter

[Party] argues [Contract 1 / an illegal act] taints [the claim on Contract 2], asking per Euro-Diam (1) is there a relevant foreign illegality, and (2) is it sufficiently connected to [the claim]?

  • Where it arises: [an illegal manner of performance not contractually required] (Howard v Shirlstar), [omitting a needed licence] (Skilling), or [a related illegal transaction] (Euro-Diam).
  • Singapore status: per Teng Wen-Chung, Euro-Diam cannot be accepted "unqualified", as [Bowmakers reliance] must be re-examined under Ochroid, and [Beresford's public conscience test] is not Singapore law.
  • Theoretical basis: tainting operates via (a) [the proper law] (Forsyth, cited in Teng) or (b) [forum international public policy], which decides Step 2.
  • Strategy: resisting [Contract 1] invites tainting of [Contract 2], so consider conceding [the smaller claim].
⚡ Base facts · 6 of 7M6
Granit says that Mr Halim's engagement taints the Supply Contract. What is the answer on these facts?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Never let the threshold end the answer: say it is unclear, assume it is met and go on. Which law's principles decide the connection is unresolved. If tainting is part of the lex fori, Singapore's principles decide. If it is part of the proper law, that law's do, and the proper law that counts is that of the contract sued on. Give the result under each.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.6 :: Which Law's Principles?

Unresolved, as [Teng / Baker v BCS / Surewin] all involved [Singapore-law contracts]; per Prof Chong, if tainting is part of [the lex fori], Singapore's principles decide, and if of [the proper law], that law's do.

  • Which proper law: per Chong (seminar), that of [Contract 2, the claim sued on], not of [Contract 1, the tainting transaction].
  • Submission (C&Y; Forsyth): apply [the proper law]'s principles unless [the lex fori's] rise to overriding mandatory rules or international policy, though this raises an incidental question on [the related transaction's legality].
⚡ Base facts · 7 of 7M7
Granit also wants its deposit back. Perrin points to the Supply Contract to keep it. May Perrin rely on a contract that Ralli makes partly unenforceable?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per Esben, a defendant may rely on the arrangement against a claim for the return of money unless the outcome would stultify comity. Keeping a deposit paid under a contract whose first two shipments were lawfully delivered gives effect to nothing unlawful. This is a one-line point.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.10.7 :: Stultification

Per Esben Finance, [Defendant] may rely on [the Foster / Ralli arrangement] against [an unjust enrichment claim] unless the outcome would stultify comity, which it [does / does not] as [reliance merely explains the payments / gives effect to the illegal performance].

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
⚡ BIG IDEA

Two contracts and three countries' laws, with a different illegality route for each rule. Label the proper law, the forum and the place of performance first: the Ruritanian ban then goes to Ralli, where the reading decides Granit's counterclaim, and the influence deal fails under its own proper law or under Lemenda, so Mr Halim loses either way. The move that decides the US$2 million: beating Mr Halim gives Granit the first part of step 1 of tainting; if a public policy breach is serious enough, which is open, the claim then turns on whether Singapore or Utopian principles judge the connection.

  1. 1
    Map the laws and the routes M1

    Granit pleads illegality, so list the routes: the proper law, forum international public policy, Foster, Lemenda, Ralli, tainting and reliance as a defence. Only three laws can matter: the proper law, the forum and the place of performance (for Foster, the place where the act is really meant to happen); per Sim See Kee, illegality at the place of signing or at a party's home is irrelevant. For the Supply Contract they are Utopian law (clause 14), Singapore law, and Ruritanian law because clause 5 requires delivery at Port Ruri, not because Granit is Ruritanian or state-owned. Clause 14 stands although Utopia has no link with the deal: a chosen law needs no connection (Per Peh Teck Quee), and nothing suggests it was chosen to dodge a rule. The engagement letter has no clause, so its proper law must be found before Mr Halim's claim is answered.

  2. 2
    Proper law illegality first; Foster is out M2

    Ask first whether the law broken is the proper law itself: if so, it bars enforcement (Per Kahler and Zivnostenka). For the Supply Contract it is not, because nothing in Utopian law makes the contract unlawful and the ban is Ruritanian. So the ban can only work through Foster or Ralli. Foster is out: intention at formation is the crux (Per Magdeev), and the ban came on 1 April 2025, after signing, so no one intended to break it. For the engagement letter the answer may differ, if its proper law is Ruritanian.

  3. 3
    The missing shipments: Ralli on each reading M5

    Per Ralli Brothers, a contract is unenforceable “in so far as” performance is unlawful at the contractual place of performance, whatever the proper law, and the ban makes the delivery that clause 5 requires at Port Ruri a crime. Per C&Y, Ralli has three readings, and here they differ because the proper law is not Singapore law (Per Ryder Industries). Reading (1), the independent rule (Per Esben; start here, as Prof Chong finds it arguably preferable): delivery at Port Ruri is unenforceable, so Granit's US$900,000 counterclaim fails, though Granit will say that a lawful port under the proper law means no unlawful act is demanded in Ruritania, which would let the counterclaim succeed on this reading too. Reading (2), frustration under the proper law, to which Peh Teck Quee leaned: Utopian law requires delivery at the nearest lawful port once the buyer asks, and Granit asked for Port Arca, so Perrin's refusal is a breach and the counterclaim succeeds. Singapore's own frustration rule is irrelevant, as Singapore law is only the forum. Reading (3), comity abstention, is supported by dicta (Toprak; Magdeev), but per Peh Teck Quee Ralli has “nothing to do with” public policy.

  4. 4
    The price for the two delivered shipments M5

    Granit also pleads the ban against the US$2 million price. Ralli bites only “in so far as” a required act is unlawful where it must be done: the two shipments were delivered lawfully before the ban, and nothing bans paying for them. So the price claim asks the court to enforce nothing unlawful, and Ralli probably does not touch it. Say “probably”, because Esben leaves unclear whether Ralli strikes the whole contract or only part (Per C&Y). The real threat to the price is tainting.

  5. 5
    The engagement letter's proper law L6

    With no clause and nothing that implies a choice, the engagement is governed by the law of its closest and most real connection (Per Bonython; Pacific Recreation). Per Prof Chong, the strongest factor is usually where both parties perform: Mr Halim uses his influence in Ruritania and is paid there, and he lives there. For Singapore, the letter was signed there and Perrin is based there, but per Pacific Recreation the place of contracting matters little unless performance is also there. So Ruritanian law is probably the proper law. Run Singapore law as the alternative, because the next step gives the same result under both.

  6. 6
    Mr Halim's commission: proper law, then Lemenda M2M4

    If Ruritanian law governs, the engagement is void under its own proper law, and that bars enforcement (Per Kahler and Zivnostenka). If Singapore law governs, apply Lemenda: a commission for buying influence is not enforced if it offends both a forum policy founded on general morality and the same policy where the influence is to be used, here Ruritania. Both are met, because Singapore shares Ruritania's policy, so Shaikh Faisal does not help Mr Halim, and the Westacre doubt does not arise, as the proper law is then the forum itself. It is not Foster, as no written law is broken, and not forum fundamental policy, as buying influence offends only domestic policy (per Phillips J in Lemenda). Mr Halim fails either way.

  7. 7
    Tainting: the price of beating Mr Halim M6

    Granit says the engagement taints Perrin's claim, asking per Euro-Diam (1) is there a relevant foreign illegality and (2) is it sufficiently connected to the claim. Step 1 asks whether Singapore would enforce the engagement (Per Surewin), so Perrin's win against Mr Halim gives Granit the first part of step 1; Perrin should consider conceding the US$300,000 commission. Whether a breach of public policy alone, the Lemenda kind, is serious enough is unclear (Prof Chong): say so, assume it is, and go on. Which law's principles decide step 2 is unresolved. Per Prof Chong, if tainting is part of the lex fori, Singapore principles apply, find no sufficient connection, and Perrin recovers the US$2 million. If it is part of the proper law, the law that counts is that of the contract sued on (Per Chong (seminar)), Utopian law, which finds a connection, so the claim is barred; Ruritania's view on the connection does not count.

  8. 8
    The deposit: reliance as a defence M7

    Granit wants its US$500,000 deposit back, and Perrin relies on the Supply Contract to keep it. Per Esben, a defendant may rely on a Ralli arrangement against a claim for the return of money unless the outcome would stultify comity. On the independent rule reading, where Ralli leaves the last two shipments unenforceable, keeping the deposit does not stultify comity: the contract only explains why the deposit was paid, and the two shipments were delivered lawfully. On the frustration reading nothing is unenforceable, so no illegality point arises on the deposit. One line is enough.

Per C&Y (and Day), Ralli is (1) an independent conflicts rule, (2) frustration under [the proper law], or (3) comity-based abstention, and [the result] turns on [the reading].

  • (1) Independent rule (start here): per Esben, Dicey's rule rooted in comity, catching [supervening] and initial illegality alike, and per Prof Chong arguably preferable as [the later, more unequivocal] SGCA ruling.
  • (2) Frustration (alternative): Peh Teck Quee leaned to it, declining Ralli where [the ban pre-dated the contract], so ask whether [the proper law] frustrates or permits [delivery elsewhere].
  • (3) Comity abstention: supported by dicta (Toprak; Magdeev), but per Peh Teck Quee Ralli has "nothing to do with" [public policy], unlike [Foster].
  • When it matters: per Ryder Industries, only where [the proper law] is not [the lex fori], as Singapore domestic law frustrates [the contract] anyway.

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
  1. 1
    What changes, and what stays

    The ban now came first: it has been in force since 1 December 2024, six weeks before the Supply Contract was signed. Perrin knew of it and planned to ship with false year plates; Granit had not heard of it. On the base facts Foster was out because no one intended to break the ban; now Perrin did. Mr Halim's claim and the tainting analysis stay the same.

  2. 2
    Foster bars Perrin's price claim M3

    Per Foster v Driscoll and Regazzoni (in Singapore, Patriot v Lam Hong; Esben), a contract whose real object is to break a friendly state's law inside that state is unenforceable. Intention at formation is the crux (Per Magdeev): at signing Perrin meant to bring old machines into Ruritania, a crime there, behind false year plates. The object is dominant, because the planned breach is the very delivery the contract is for (Per Magdeev). Per Royal Boskalis, a unilateral intention bars only its holder, so Perrin, the claimant, cannot recover the US$2 million. The false plates are evidence of that intention, not a tort claim, and Granit's ignorance goes to whose intention it was, not to whether a contract was formed.

  3. 3
    Granit's counterclaim: past Foster, but still facing Ralli M3M5

    Innocent Granit may still sue (Per Royal Boskalis; Ang v Lyu; Surewin), though not for an order compelling the unlawful delivery. Foster and Ralli are separate rules, so ask again whether delivery at Port Ruri can be enforced. Reading (1) (Per Esben): Ralli catches initial illegality too, so delivery at Port Ruri is unenforceable and the counterclaim fails. Reading (2): Peh Teck Quee declined Ralli for a ban that pre-dated the contract, so the proper law decides; Utopian law requires delivery at the nearest lawful port, Port Arca, which Granit asked for, so Perrin is in breach and the counterclaim succeeds.

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
  1. 1
    What changes, and what stays

    A new Foster plea: from the start Granit planned to declare the machines to Ruritanian customs at half their value, a crime under a Customs Code in force since 2015. Perrin's sales manager knew before signing, but Perrin took no part. Granit pleads its own plan against Perrin's price claim. The Ralli, Lemenda and tainting answers stay as they were.

  2. 2
    Foster reaches a revenue law, whatever the proper law M3

    Per Foster v Driscoll and Regazzoni, a contract whose real object is to evade customs in a friendly state is unenforceable, and here the plan was held at signing. Per Patriot and Regazzoni, a revenue law counts, because refusing to help break it is recognition, not enforcement. Per Ang v Lyu and Surewin, Foster is forum public policy, so it applies under Utopian law as the proper law, whatever Utopian law thinks of foreign revenue laws; the Code is a foreign law, so it comes in only through the illegality routes, not as a Singapore mandatory rule. Per Surewin, the act must be contemplated within Ruritania, though per Foster and Regazzoni not necessarily at the stipulated place, so a false declaration at customs rather than at the depot still counts. Per Magdeev, the plan must also be the dominant object: Perrin will say it was a side feature of a real sale at a real price, and if so Foster bars no one.

  3. 3
    Who is barred: knowledge against participation M3

    Per Royal Boskalis, a unilateral intention bars only its holder, so Granit cannot use its own plan against Perrin unless Perrin shares the intention. Whether mere knowledge is enough is open. If it is (Soetanto), Perrin is barred. If active participation is needed (Dimplex Gems, which doubts Soetanto), Perrin, which took no part, is not barred, and as Soetanto is doubted, Perrin probably defeats this plea. Then test Foster against Granit as claimant: Granit holds the intention, so Perrin can plead Foster against Granit's counterclaims if the plan was the dominant object. Perrin's line on dominance cuts both ways: if the plan was not dominant, Foster bars Granit's counterclaims no more than Perrin's claim.

  4. 4
    The variation: Perrin issued the invoices M3

    If Perrin's sales manager issued the half-value invoices, Perrin took an active part, so the doubt about its mental state goes and Foster can bar its price claim. Its remaining argument is the dominant object: cheating customs was a side feature of a real sale, not “central to the adventure” (Per Magdeev). This is not Ralli, because the contract does not require a false invoice.

5Scorecards: weigh the factors

Prof Chong rewards applying facts to factor tests. Sort each fact, then answer the verdict question. These use the base facts unless a line says “Suppose”.

M1 Sort the factors: Which route does this fact open?

Each line is a fact. Does it open Foster (an intention at signing to break a foreign law), Ralli (a required act made unlawful where it must be done), or neither? “Neither” includes a fact that belongs to another route. Lines marked “Suppose” are extra facts for this card only.

After signing, Ruritania makes it a crime to import the machines that clause 5 says must be delivered at Port Ruri.
Ralli. Supervening illegality of an act that the contract requires, at the contractual place of performance. Intention is irrelevant. C2.10.5 :: Illegal Performance
Ruritanian public policy, with no statute behind it, condemns paying for influence over a state-owned company.
Neither. Foreign public policy alone goes to Lemenda, and it works only if Singapore shares the policy. Foster and Ralli are for written law. C2.10.1 :: Framework: Foster vs Ralli vs Lemenda
Suppose (Twist 3): from the start Granit planned to under-declare the machines to Ruritanian customs.
Foster. A written law, in force at signing, and a plan to break it inside that state. A revenue law counts. C2.10.3 :: Any Written Law
Suppose: Granit always meant to drive the machines on into Elbonia, also a friendly state, where importing them is a crime. The contract names only Port Ruri.
Foster. The unlawful act must be contemplated inside the foreign state, but not necessarily at the stipulated place. The court looks at the real object. C2.10.3 :: Territorial, Not the Stipulated Place
Suppose: both parties agreed at signing to label the machines as farm tractors to pay less Ruritanian duty. In the end Perrin labelled them correctly.
Foster. Intention at formation decides, even if the plan was never carried out. C2.10.3 :: Wicked Intention Is the Crux
Suppose: clause 6 requires Granit to pay the price at a bank in Port Ruri, and after signing Ruritania makes it a crime to pay foreign sellers.
Ralli. The payment itself is a required act, now unlawful at the place where the contract says it must be done. C2.10.5 :: Illegal Performance
Suppose: after signing, Ruritania forbids its companies to send money abroad without central bank consent. The price is payable in Singapore.
Neither. What a debtor must do at home to be able to pay is a preparatory step. The required act, payment in Singapore, is lawful where it must be done. C2.10.5 :: Preparatory Steps Excluded
Suppose: the Supply Contract was signed in Elbonia, where selling used machinery without a dealer's licence is an offence.
Neither. Illegality at the place of contracting is irrelevant. Only the proper law, the forum and the place of performance count. C2.10.1 :: Irrelevant Laws
Suppose: clause 14 chose Ruritanian law, and the ban makes contracts for banned machines void.
Neither. The law broken is then the proper law itself. That is proper law illegality, and Foster and the parties' intentions are irrelevant. C2.10.1 :: Route A: Proper Law
⚡ Scorecard 1 · the verdictM1
On the base facts, which route does the import ban open against the Supply Contract?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Ralli looks to action, Foster to intention. The ban is a written law, so it is not Lemenda. Ruritanian law is the law of the place of performance, not the proper law, so it is not proper law illegality. No one intended at signing to break a ban that did not exist, so it is not Foster.

M6 Sort the factors: Does Mr Halim's engagement taint the Supply Contract?

Each line is a fact offered on Granit's tainting plea. Does it count towards a taint, does it not count, or is it a point on which both views must be run? Lines marked “Suppose” are extra facts for this card only.

Singapore would refuse to enforce Mr Halim's engagement, under its proper law or under Lemenda.
Counts towards a taint. Step 1 asks whether there is a relevant illegality, which includes asking whether Singapore would enforce the related contract. C2.10.6 :: Act or Transaction
The engagement offends public policy only. It is not a crime, and no bribe is alleged.
Open: run both views. Not every breach is serious enough. Whether a Lemenda breach meets the threshold is unclear. Say so, assume it is met, and go on. C2.10.4 :: Lemenda as a Taint?
Utopian law, which governs the Supply Contract, finds a sufficient connection. Singapore law does not.
Open: run both views. Which law's principles decide the connection is unresolved: the lex fori or the proper law. The result differs, so run both. C2.10.6 :: Which Law's Principles?
Ruritanian law, the law of the place of delivery, finds no sufficient connection.
Does not count. Step 2 is for the lex fori or the proper law of the contract sued on. The view of the place of performance on the connection does not decide it. C2.10.6 :: Which Law's Principles?
Suppose: the engagement letter is governed by Arcadian law, and Arcadian law would find a sufficient connection.
Does not count. The proper law that counts is that of the contract sued on, the Supply Contract, not that of the tainting transaction. C2.10.6 :: Which Law's Principles?
Suppose: Mr Halim's only wrong was to act in Ruritania without registering as a sales agent, which carries a fine of R$200.
Does not count. An administrative or minor breach does not taint, as with the customs approval missed in Ryder Industries. C2.10.6 :: Insufficient: Administrative
Suppose: Mr Halim bribed Granit's directors, a crime in Ruritania punished by prison.
Counts towards a taint. A serious breach of a prohibition at the place of performance qualifies at step 1. The connection at step 2 must still be shown. C2.10.6 :: Sufficiently Serious
⚡ Scorecard 2 · the verdictM6
On the base facts, does the tainting plea defeat Perrin's US$2 million claim?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Step 1 is met if a Lemenda breach is serious enough, which is unclear, so assume it and go on. At step 2 the facts give a connection under Utopian law only. If tainting works as part of the lex fori, Singapore principles apply and Perrin recovers. If it works as part of the proper law of the contract sued on, Utopian principles apply and the claim is barred. Teng Wen-Chung said only that Euro-Diam cannot be accepted unqualified.

6Remember

🧠 FOR THE EXAM
  • Only the proper law, the forum and the place of performance can matter (for Foster, the place where the act is really meant to happen); the place of signing or a party's home does not (Per Sim See Kee).
  • Ralli catches a ban on an act the contract requires where it must be done, made after signing or (on the Esben reading) before; Foster needs an intention at signing to break it; where the proper law is not Singapore law, run Ralli's readings, as they can give opposite results.
  • Ralli bites only “in so far as” a required act is unlawful where it must be done: it probably does not reach the price of deliveries made lawfully before the ban, and it does not reach delivery at a lawful port that the contract lets the buyer name, once the buyer names it.
  • Foreign public policy with no statute behind it is Lemenda, but find the proper law first: if that law condemns the deal, the contract fails under its own proper law.
  • Beating the intermediary's claim gives the other side the first part of step 1 of tainting (whether a public policy breach is serious enough is open); at step 2 run Singapore principles and the proper law of the contract sued on, with a result under each.
  • Foster bars only the holder of the intention; whether mere knowledge is enough is open (Soetanto against Dimplex Gems), and the illegal object must be dominant.

Pascoe v Halvard

Written by Claude for the drill and law reviewed. Gemini (prompt v1) wrote a guide to it; the guide was checked (3 corrections) and feeds the walkthrough. Gemini's file: law302_question_2_review_plain_english_study_gui.

Answers:

1Base facts

🧩 HYPOTHETICAL
Pascoe v Halvard

Halvard Optics Pte Ltd is a Singapore incorporated company with its head office in Singapore. It makes all its camera lenses at its plant in Arcadia and ships them from there. Pascoe Agencies Ltd is incorporated in Elbonia.

By an Agency Agreement signed in 2019, Halvard appointed Pascoe as its sole sales agent in Elbonia. Pascoe found buyers in Elbonia and was paid its commission there. Clause 21 reads:

“This Agreement is governed by Arcadian law, save that clause 9 (the Agent's duties under Elbonian data protection rules) is governed by Elbonian law.”

Before signing, Halvard's lawyer emailed Pascoe: “We use Arcadian law because it gives agents no termination payment.” Halvard uses the same Arcadian law form for its agents in nine countries. Pascoe says that it signed because Halvard's sales director told it, at a meeting in Elbonia, that no other agent would be appointed in the region. That was untrue.

In 2025 Halvard ended the agency on three months' notice. Pascoe sues Halvard in the General Division for compensation under the Elbonian Commercial Agents Act. Halvard relies on clause 21. Pascoe replies that clause 21 is not bona fide, not legal and against public policy; that the false statement means clause 21 does not bind it; and that leaving an agent with nothing after six years offends Singapore public policy. Assume that the court has jurisdiction.

Advise Pascoe.

ℹ ASSUME
  1. The Elbonian Commercial Agents Act gives an agent two years' commission when the principal ends the agency. The Act says that this right “cannot be excluded by contract”.
  2. Arcadian law gives an agent no termination payment. Under Arcadian law a statement made before a contract has no effect unless it is repeated in the written contract.
  3. Singapore law gives a commercial agent no termination payment.
  4. Pascoe read and signed every page of the Agreement.
  5. Ending the agency on three months' notice was allowed by the Agreement under both Arcadian law and Elbonian law.
✔ ROUND 1 · WHICH MENU BOXES?Note the boxes you would tick, then tap to compare.

Write from these boxes

  • L2
    Express choice of law clause. Clause 21 is an express choice of Arcadian law. It is virtually conclusive unless it is not bona fide, not legal or against public policy, and Singapore law as the lex fori tests those limits.
  • L4
    Law chosen to dodge another country's rule. The email says Arcadian law was used because it gives agents no termination payment. That is the evasion attack: the clause falls only if dodging the law that would otherwise govern was the sole purpose.
  • L6
    SCORECARD · Objective proper law: closest and most real connection. If clause 21 is struck out, the answer skips implied choice and needs the objective proper law. Pascoe's work and its commission are in Elbonia, so the weighing has to be done.
  • L9
    Other attacks on the clause; capacity. Two attacks from this box. Pascoe says the false statement knocks out clause 21 itself, which is the infection test. And clause 21 splits the governing law, which is allowed if the split is coherent.
  • K8
    Forum public policy; renvoi. Pascoe's last resort is Singapore public policy against the Arcadian rule. Only fundamental public policy counts, and it is narrower than domestic policy.

Decoys: tempting, but wrong on these facts

  • L3
    Floating or one-sided choice of law clause. Tempting because clause 21 names two laws. Wrong because both are fixed at signing, each for a defined part of the contract. That is a split, not a floating choice.
  • M1
    Illegality: pick the route. Tempting because a foreign statute that “cannot be excluded” stands against Halvard. Wrong because nothing makes the making or performance of the Agreement unlawful in Elbonia. The Act gives a money right, which exists only if Elbonian law governs.
  • K7
    A Singapore statute said to override the chosen law. Tempting because the Act calls itself mandatory. Wrong because K7 is for a Singapore statute that overrides the chosen law. A foreign statute applies in a Singapore court only as part of the proper law.
  • L5
    No clause: implied choice. Tempting if clause 21 falls: the Arcadian plant and the Arcadian form might imply Arcadian law. Wrong because a failed express choice is not rescued by an inferred one. The answer goes straight to stage 3.

Fair to tick but not needed: L1 Starter: the proper law and its three stages, K1 Characterise the issue

Application questions · base facts

⚡ Base facts · 1 of 7L2
Pascoe attacks clause 21 as “not bona fide, not legal and against public policy”. How should the answer treat the three limbs?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per Peh Teck Quee, applying Vita Food, the choice is virtually conclusive unless not bona fide, legal or consistent with public policy, each tested by the lex fori on objective intention. Per C&Y, “legal” is of unclear meaning and the public policy limb duplicates the general reservation, so the attacking party leads with bona fides.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.1 :: Limbs (b) and (c)

Per C&Y, "legal" is of unclear meaning and the public policy limb duplicates [the general reservation] (C2.10.2), so [the attacking party] leads with [bona fides].

⚡ Base facts · 2 of 7L4
The email says that Arcadian law was used “because it gives agents no termination payment”. Does that defeat clause 21?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per Peh Teck Quee, choosing a law to evade another country's law defeats the clause only if evasion was the sole purpose. A genuine connection with the chosen law, such as the place of manufacture, and a second reason, such as one law for the whole agency network, point to a bona fide choice. Give both sides, then a view.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.2 :: The Argument

Per Peh Teck Quee, choosing [law X] to evade [the moneylending / exchange control / consumer laws of country Y] defeats the clause only if evasion was the sole purpose.

  • "Another law": per C&Y, usually [the OPL], but possibly [a forum mandatory rule] (Golden Acres), whose evasion fails twice: [the rule] applies anyway and [the clause] is struck out.
⚡ Base facts · 3 of 7L6
Suppose the court does strike out clause 21 for evasion. What governs the Agreement?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

A choice that is not bona fide is struck out completely, unlike the UCTA overlay. The parties turned their minds to the governing law and failed, so inferring a choice is artificial and the answer goes to stage 3. The agent's performance and its commission are in Elbonia.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.8 :: Skip Stage 2

Per Shanghai Turbo and The Iran Vojdan, as [the parties] turned their minds to [the governing law] and failed ([not bona fide / floating / infected]), inferring a choice is "artificial", so go to Stage 3.

  • Low stakes: per Pacific Recreation, skipping Stage 2 is "not as significant a step as it seems", as [the same factors] recur at [Stage 3].
⚡ Base facts · 4 of 7L2
Suppose clause 21 stands. Can Pascoe still claim under the Elbonian Act because its protection “cannot be excluded by contract”?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

The proper law governs the effect and discharge of the contract. Elbonian law is neither the proper law nor the law of the forum. The law of a place of performance comes in only through the illegality rules, and nothing here makes any act of performance unlawful in Elbonia.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.1.1 :: Scope

Per C&Y, the proper law governs [interpretation / incorporation of terms / performance / discharge], material validity ([duress / misrepresentation]: CIMB) and illegality under it (C2.10.1), and per s 3(1) FLPA its [limitation period] applies (C1.5).

  • Not covered: [formation] (C2.6), [form] (C2.7), [capacity] (C2.8) and procedure, e.g., [burden of proof / arguably quantum] (C1.2 to C1.4), unlike Art 9 Hague Principles, which extends to [burden of proof / pre-contractual obligations].
⚡ Base facts · 5 of 7L9
Pascoe says that the false statement about exclusivity knocks out clause 21 as well. Does it?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

The choice of law clause is separable. Per C&Y, the crux is whether the vitiating factor leaves no consensus on the clause itself. A misstatement about the subject matter affects the contract, not the agreement on the governing law. A merely disputed misrepresentation leaves the chosen law applying as if the contract were valid (CIMB). Under Arcadian law the statement has no effect.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.3 :: The Test

Per C&Y, the crux is whether [the vitiating factor] leaves no consensus on the clause itself, not whether [the contract] is void or voidable; if infected, [the OPL] governs material validity.

⚡ Base facts · 6 of 7L9
Clause 21 puts clause 9 under Elbonian law. Does that help Pascoe to reach the Elbonian Act?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per Libyan Arab Foreign Bank, one law may govern one part of a contract and another law the rest. A split is not inferred readily, but here it is express and coherent: one defined clause, one law. It does not widen the reach of Elbonian law.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.6 :: Split / Dépeçage

Per Libyan Arab Foreign Bank, [law A] may govern [one part] and [law B] [the rest] (cf Art 2(2) Hague Principles), but per Kahler a split is not inferred "readily or without good reason", parties expecting one law (Enka).

  • Coherence: the split must be internally coherent, so not [different laws on repudiation] depending on [which party is innocent].
⚡ Base facts · 7 of 7K8
Pascoe's last argument is that leaving an agent with nothing after six years offends Singapore public policy. Will it work?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

The court refuses a foreign rule only if it infringes Singapore's fundamental public policy. A rule that would be objectionable domestically is not enough, and here Singapore domestic law is the same as Arcadian law. This is the last resort and it fails.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C1.8 :: Fundamental Public Policy

Per C&Y, the court refuses [the offending foreign rule] or [the contract] only if it infringes Singapore's fundamental (international) public policy, narrower than domestic policy, so [the rule / contract] being [void / objectionable] domestically is insufficient (cf Art 11(3) Hague Principles: "manifestly incompatible").

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
⚡ BIG IDEA

Halvard chose Arcadian law and admitted why: it gives agents nothing on termination. The hypo tests whether that admission strikes out clause 21, which needs evasion as the sole purpose, and whether any other argument helps Pascoe: infection by the false statement, the clause 9 split, the Act's own words, or Singapore public policy. On balance each fails and Arcadian law probably governs. Pascoe's only route to two years' commission is to knock out clause 21, so that Elbonian law, probably the objective proper law, governs.

  1. 1
    The issue and clause 21 L2

    Pascoe's claim to two years' commission turns on the effect and discharge of the Agreement, which its proper law governs (Per Amin Rasheed). Clause 21 expressly chooses Arcadian law, which gives an agent nothing on termination. Per Peh Teck Quee, applying Vita Food, the choice is virtually conclusive unless it is not bona fide, not legal or against public policy, each tested by Singapore law as the lex fori on objective intention. Per C&Y, “legal” is of unclear meaning and the public policy limb repeats the general reservation, so Pascoe leads with bona fides. Arcadian law needs no connection with the Agreement (Per Peh Teck Quee), though here it has one.

  2. 2
    Bona fides: was evasion the sole purpose? L4

    Per Peh Teck Quee, choosing a law to evade another country's law defeats the clause only if evasion was the sole purpose. Pascoe's case first: the email is direct evidence that Arcadian law was chosen to avoid a termination payment, which Elbonian law, the likely objective proper law, would give. Halvard's reply: it makes all its lenses at its Arcadian plant, a genuine link like the place of booking in Peh Teck Quee, and it uses the same Arcadian law form for its agents in nine countries, which shows a second purpose: one law for the whole network. So evasion was probably not the sole purpose, and clause 21 probably stands. The Act's words “cannot be excluded by contract” do not change this: the lex fori tests the limits on a choice, and those words bind only if Elbonian law governs.

  3. 3
    If clause 21 fell: straight to the objective proper law L6

    If the court did find evasion the sole purpose, clause 21 would be struck out completely, not merely overlaid as under s 27(2) of UCTA. Per Shanghai Turbo and The Iran Vojdan, parties who tried to choose a law and failed get no implied choice, so the Arcadian plant and form cannot found one: skip stage 2. Per Bonython, the court then looks for the closest and most real connection, and per Prof Chong the strongest argument is usually the place where both parties perform. Both parties perform in Elbonia: Pascoe found buyers there, and Halvard paid its commission there. Halvard's Singapore head office and Arcadian plant point elsewhere but weigh less. Elbonian law is probably the objective proper law, so the Act would apply as part of it and give Pascoe two years' commission.

  4. 4
    While clause 21 stands, the Act drops out L2

    With clause 21 standing, a payment on termination is a matter for Arcadian law as the proper law (Per C&Y, the proper law governs performance and discharge). A foreign statute that gives a money right applies here only as part of the proper law, whatever it says about exclusion, and Elbonian law is neither the proper law nor the law of the forum. The overriding statutes that a Singapore court lays over a foreign proper law are Singapore's own, not Elbonia's. A place of performance comes in only through the illegality rules (Foster, Ralli, Lemenda). Those rules are pleaded to resist a claim on the contract, so they cannot give Pascoe a payment, and in any case nothing makes the making or performance of the Agreement unlawful in Elbonia.

  5. 5
    The false statement does not infect clause 21 L9

    Clause 21 is separable from the rest of the Agreement (Per Maldives Airports), so per CIMB a misrepresentation that vitiates the Agreement does not necessarily infect it. Per C&Y, the crux is whether the false statement leaves no consensus on clause 21 itself, not whether the Agreement is voidable. A statement that no other agent would be appointed goes to the bargain, not to the governing law, and Pascoe read and signed every page, so this is not a case like non est factum that infects everything. Per CIMB, a merely disputed misrepresentation leaves the chosen law applying as if the contract were valid. So clause 21 probably survives, and Arcadian law decides the statement's effect: a statement not repeated in the written contract has none. If the clause were infected, it would fail like a choice that is not bona fide: skip stage 2, and the objective proper law, probably Elbonian, would govern.

  6. 6
    The split does not widen Elbonian law L9

    Clause 21 puts clause 9, the data protection duties, under Elbonian law. Per Libyan Arab Foreign Bank, one law may govern one part of a contract and another law the rest; per Kahler a split is not inferred readily, but this one is express and coherent: one defined clause, one law. It is not a floating clause, because both laws were fixed at signing, each for a defined part. Each law governs only its own part, and ending the agency is outside clause 9, so termination stays under Arcadian law.

  7. 7
    Last resort: Singapore public policy K8

    Pascoe says that leaving an agent with nothing after six years offends Singapore public policy. Per C&Y, the court refuses a foreign rule only if it infringes Singapore's fundamental public policy, which is narrower than domestic policy, so even a rule objectionable at home is not enough. Singapore's own law gives a commercial agent no termination payment either, so the Arcadian rule is not even objectionable domestically. The argument fails.

  8. 8
    Advice

    Put Pascoe's case first, then say why it probably fails. Clause 21 probably survives the bona fide attack, the false statement probably does not infect it, the split does not reach termination and public policy fails, so Arcadian law probably governs and Pascoe gets no termination payment. If the court found evasion the sole purpose, clause 21 would be struck out completely, Elbonian law would probably govern as the objective proper law, and the Act would give Pascoe two years' commission.

2Twist 1

🧩 TWIST 1

Go back to the base facts and change clause 21.

Suppose that clause 21 read instead:

“This Agreement and all disputes arising out of it are governed by Arcadian law or Elbonian law, as the Principal elects by notice once a dispute has arisen.”

When Pascoe threatened to sue, Halvard gave notice electing Arcadian law.

ℹ ASSUME
  1. A clause that lets one party pick the governing law after a dispute has arisen is valid under Elbonian law. It is invalid under Arcadian law and under Singapore law.
✔ ROUND 1 · WHICH MENU BOXES?Note the boxes you would tick, then tap to compare.

Write from these boxes

  • L3
    Floating or one-sided choice of law clause. No law is fixed at signing. One party picks it later. That is a floating, one-sided clause, and the laws disagree on whether it is valid, so the first question is which law tests it.

Decoys: tempting, but wrong on these facts

  • L5
    No clause: implied choice. Tempting if the clause is void: Halvard's election and its Arcadian plant might imply Arcadian law. Wrong because parties who tried to choose and failed do not get an inferred choice. Skip stage 2.
  • N6
    Party autonomy: does the contract's chosen law govern the tort?. Tempting because of the words “all disputes arising out of it”. Wrong because N6 asks whether a law clause reaches a tort claim, and Pascoe's claim is for a payment under the Agreement.

Fair to tick but not needed: L2 Express choice of law clause, L4 Law chosen to dodge another country's rule, L6 SCORECARD · Objective proper law: closest and most real connection, L9 Other attacks on the clause; capacity

Application questions · twist 1

⚡ Twist 1 · 1 of 4L3
Is the new clause 21 valid?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per C&Y, the Shanghai Turbo High Court on balance used the lex fori, while The Iran Vojdan used the objective proper law. Under Singapore law the clause is invalid even with an election mechanism. If the objective proper law permits floating clauses, the clause is valid and the elected law governs. Argue both and give the result under each.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.5 :: Which Law Tests Validity? (argue both)

Per C&Y, the Shanghai Turbo HC on balance used the lex fori (also testing [both candidate laws]), whereas The Iran Vojdan used [the OPL] (German law: void as small print, though it permits floating clauses; Iranian, presumed English: void as floating).

  • Lex fori (−): per Prof Chong, under Singapore law [cl X] is invalid even with [an election mechanism], so [the OPL] governs.
  • OPL (+): per Prof Chong, if [the OPL, e.g., law Z] permits floating clauses, [cl X] is valid and [law A] governs once [party] [elects / sues first].
⚡ Twist 1 · 2 of 4L3
What is the result for Pascoe's claim under each route?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Striking out the clause leaves the contract under its objective proper law. It does not bring in the lex fori as the governing law, and stage 2 is skipped. On the other route the clause works as written, so the law Halvard elected governs, subject to the Vita Food limits.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.5 :: Contract Survives

Per Shanghai Turbo and The Iran Vojdan, striking out [cl X] leaves [the contract] under [the OPL], though per C&Y, if [no law at all] was intended, "a contract without a law is no contract at all".

⚡ Twist 1 · 3 of 4L3
Base clause 21 also named two laws. Why is this clause floating when that one was not?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

A contract cannot exist in a legal vacuum (Amin Rasheed). A clause that applies one law or another on one party's later election has no law at the start and is of no legal effect under Singapore law. A split fixes both laws from the start.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.5 :: Floating Clause Void

As contracts cannot exist "in a legal vacuum" (Amin Rasheed), cl [X] applying [law A or law B] on [one party's election / a future event] is "meaningless" and of no legal effect (Shanghai Turbo), so skip Stage 2 (C2.2.8).

  • No election mechanism: as in Shanghai Turbo (cl 17: "laws of Singapore/or People's Republic of China"), [the missing mechanism] adds to [the uncertainty].
⚡ Twist 1 · 4 of 4L3
How would it differ if clause 21 said: “This Agreement is governed by Elbonian law. The Principal may by notice elect that it be governed instead by Arcadian law”?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

In theory a floating clause has no law until it crystallises, while a change varies an existing law. Per C&Y the line is fine. Parties may change the proper law (Kredietbank), but whether the lex fori or the original proper law decides if the change is allowed is open. Do not call an option to change a floating clause without saying why.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.5 :: Distinguish a Change of Proper Law (C2.2.6)

In theory [a floating clause] has no law until crystallisation (void), while [a change] varies an existing law (valid), but per C&Y the line is fine, as [the OPL] operates meanwhile in both.

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
  1. 1
    What changes, and what stays

    Clause 21 now names Arcadian law or Elbonian law, as Halvard elects once a dispute has arisen, and Halvard elected Arcadian law when Pascoe threatened to sue. The other base facts stay: the email, the Arcadian plant, the nine-country form, and Pascoe's work and commission in Elbonia. In the base a law was fixed at signing, so the attack was on its purpose; now no law is fixed until Halvard elects, so the first question is whether the clause is valid at all, and by which law. The words “all disputes arising out of it” raise no tort point, because Pascoe claims a payment under the Agreement.

  2. 2
    A floating clause: which law tests it? L3

    Contracts cannot exist in a legal vacuum (Amin Rasheed), so under Singapore law a clause applying one law or another on one party's later election is meaningless and of no legal effect (Shanghai Turbo). The base clause was a split, each law fixed at signing for a defined part; this one has no law at the start. Which law tests validity is open, so argue both. Per C&Y, the Shanghai Turbo High Court on balance used the lex fori, and per Prof Chong under Singapore law the clause is invalid even with an election mechanism. The Iran Vojdan used the objective proper law, and per Prof Chong, if that law permits floating clauses, the clause is valid: here the objective proper law is probably Elbonian, and Elbonian law permits it.

  3. 3
    The result under each route L3L6

    Lex fori route: the clause is void, but the Agreement survives under its objective proper law (Per Shanghai Turbo and The Iran Vojdan); it is not “no contract at all”, because the parties meant a law to govern. Stage 2 is skipped, so neither the election nor the plant implies Arcadian law, and Elbonian law probably governs: the Act applies. Objective proper law route: the clause is valid and Arcadian law governs once elected, so Pascoe must show that the election was not bona fide. It can point to the timing, as Halvard elected only once a claim was threatened, though the clause itself allowed an election only after a dispute had arisen. If the plant and the nine-country form still show another purpose, as in the base, the attack and the claim fail; if evasion was the sole purpose, the election is struck out and Elbonian law probably governs.

  4. 4
    Contrast: an option to change the law L3

    Suppose clause 21 chose Elbonian law and let Halvard elect Arcadian law instead by notice. A law then governs from the start, so in theory the notice changes an existing law, which parties may agree (Per Kredietbank v Sinotani), while a floating clause has no law until it crystallises. Per C&Y the line is fine, so do not call such an option floating without saying why. Whether the lex fori or the original proper law, Elbonian law, decides if the change is allowed is open. If it is allowed, Arcadian law governs after the notice, subject to the bona fide attack; if not, Elbonian law still governs and the Act applies.

3Twist 2

🧩 TWIST 2

Now add these facts to the base facts.

Pascoe adds two claims. It claims damages under the Misrepresentation Act for the sales director's statement. It also claims the value of its demonstration lenses, which were lost through Halvard's carelessness while stored at Halvard's service centre in Singapore. It sues for breach of clause 8, under which Halvard must keep the Agent's stock safe. Halvard relies on clause 16:

“The Principal is not liable for loss of or damage to the Agent's property in its custody, however caused.”
ℹ ASSUME
  1. Clause 16 is valid under Arcadian law and Elbonian law. Under the Unfair Contract Terms Act, assume that it would fail the test of reasonableness.
  2. Pascoe bought the lenses for its agency business. No claim is made in tort.
✔ ROUND 1 · WHICH MENU BOXES?Note the boxes you would tick, then tap to compare.

Write from these boxes

  • K7
    A Singapore statute said to override the chosen law. Two Singapore statutes are now set against a foreign proper law. Each has its own rule on its reach: the Misrepresentation Act applies only where Singapore law governs, and UCTA reaches a foreign law contract only through s 27(2).

Decoys: tempting, but wrong on these facts

  • N7
    A contract clause is raised against the tort claim. Tempting because an exclusion clause meets a careless loss. Wrong because N7 is for a contract clause raised against a tort claim. Pascoe sues on clause 8, and the facts say no tort claim is made.
  • N1
    Starter: double actionability. Tempting because a false statement usually means a tort claim and double actionability. Wrong because Pascoe claims under the Act only. Whether the Act applies is a question of the statute's reach.

Fair to tick but not needed: N10 Statutory misrepresentation; defamation; damages and limitation in tort, L6 SCORECARD · Objective proper law: closest and most real connection

Application questions · twist 2

⚡ Twist 2 · 1 of 4K7
Does the Misrepresentation Act apply to the new damages claim?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

Per JIO Minerals, the Act merely supplements common law remedies and reaches a misrepresentation only where Singapore law is the proper law of the contract. Neither route to the proper law leads to Singapore law. The place of the statement is not the reason: the Act's reach turns on whether Singapore law governs.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C1.7 :: Misrepresentation Act

per JIO Minerals, the MA reaches [misrepresentations abroad] only if [the contract] has a Singapore proper law, as it merely supplements common law remedies, so [a misrepresentation in Indonesia] under [a UAE-law contract] falls outside it.

⚡ Twist 2 · 2 of 4K7
Can Pascoe use UCTA against clause 16 while a foreign law governs the Agreement?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

UCTA spells out its own reach. Under s 27(2) it applies despite a foreign choice if the term was imposed wholly or mainly to evade the Act, or if a party dealt as consumer while habitually resident here and the essential steps were taken here. Pascoe is an Elbonian business. The evasion shown is of the Elbonian Act.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C1.7 :: Types of Mandatory Rule

[the Singapore statute] relied on by [party] is either:

  • Overriding: applies irrespective of the proper law, e.g., [export / import controls] and [s 5(2) CLA on foreign gambling contracts].
  • Conditional: per s 27(2) UCTA, UCTA applies despite [the foreign choice] if (a) [the term] was imposed wholly or mainly to evade it, or (b) [a party] dealt as consumer while habitually resident here and the essential steps for contracting were taken here, [by him or others on his behalf].
  • Contrast bona fide (C2.2.2): "wholly or mainly" is wider than "sole purpose", and [the chosen law] survives subject to the Act, whereas [a non-bona fide choice] is struck out.
  • Flip side: per s 27(1) UCTA, if [Singapore law] governs only by [the parties' choice], ss 2–7 do not apply.
⚡ Twist 2 · 3 of 4K7
How would both answers differ if clause 21 had chosen Singapore law, and that choice stood?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

With a Singapore proper law the Misrepresentation Act reaches a misrepresentation made abroad (JIO Minerals). But under s 27(1) of UCTA, where Singapore law governs only by the parties' choice, ss 2 to 7 do not apply. Without the clause the proper law would be Elbonian, so this is such a case.

  • Conditional: per s 27(2) UCTA, UCTA applies despite [the foreign choice] if (a) [the term] was imposed wholly or mainly to evade it, or (b) [a party] dealt as consumer while habitually resident here and the essential steps for contracting were taken here, [by him or others on his behalf].
  • Contrast bona fide (C2.2.2): "wholly or mainly" is wider than "sole purpose", and [the chosen law] survives subject to the Act, whereas [a non-bona fide choice] is struck out.

⚡ Twist 2 · 4 of 4K7
Suppose s 27(2)(a) of UCTA did apply. What would happen to clause 21?
1–4 choose · ↵ check
⚖ THE LAW · LAW REVIEWED

UCTA is superimposed on the chosen law, not substituted for it. “Wholly or mainly” in s 27(2) is wider than the “sole purpose” needed to defeat a choice as not bona fide, and the consequences differ.

📄 Pre-write, word for word · C2.2.7 :: Superimposed, Not Struck Out

Per s 27(2) UCTA, the Act applies despite [the law X clause] if [the clause] was imposed wholly or mainly to evade it, or [a consumer] habitually resident here dealt and the essential steps were taken here, [by him or on his behalf], [law X] then applying subject to UCTA.

📘 HOW THE ANSWER RUNSTry Round 1 and the questions first.
  1. 1
    What changes, and what stays

    The proper law analysis from the base is unchanged: Arcadian law if clause 21 stands, probably Elbonian law if it falls, and Singapore law on neither result. What is new is two claims: damages under the Misrepresentation Act for the sales director's statement, and a claim on clause 8 for the demonstration lenses lost at Halvard's Singapore service centre, met by clause 16. The question is whether two Singapore statutes reach a contract governed by a foreign law; suing in Singapore, and losing the lenses there, is not enough for either. No claim is made in tort, so double actionability and a contract clause raised against a tort claim are not in play.

  2. 2
    The Misrepresentation Act K7

    Per JIO Minerals, the Act merely supplements common law remedies, so it applies only where Singapore law governs: it reaches a misrepresentation only if the contract has a Singapore proper law. Here the proper law is Arcadian law if clause 21 stands and probably Elbonian law if it falls, so the claim fails on either result. The reason is the proper law, not the place of the statement: with a Singapore proper law the Act would reach a statement made in Elbonia.

  3. 3
    UCTA against clause 16 K7

    UCTA spells out its own reach (Per C&Y). Under s 27(2) it applies despite a foreign choice only if (a) the choice was imposed wholly or mainly to evade UCTA, or (b) a party dealt as consumer while habitually resident here and the essential steps were taken here. The email shows a wish to avoid the Elbonian Act, not UCTA, and Pascoe is an Elbonian business that bought the lenses for its agency, so neither limb fits. Clause 16 is valid under Arcadian and Elbonian law, so it stands and the lens claim fails, although it would fail the UCTA reasonableness test. Even if s 27(2)(a) applied, UCTA would be superimposed on Arcadian law and clause 21 would stand: “wholly or mainly” is wider than the “sole purpose” that strikes a choice out. Per C&Y, the law evaded may possibly be a forum rule (Golden Acres), so a choice made solely to evade UCTA might fail twice: UCTA applies and the clause is struck out.

  4. 4
    Contrast: a Singapore law clause K7

    If clause 21 had chosen Singapore law and that choice stood, the two statutes would part ways. The Misrepresentation Act would apply, even to a statement made in Elbonia, because Singapore law would be the proper law (Per JIO Minerals). But per s 27(1) of UCTA, where Singapore law governs only by the parties' choice, ss 2 to 7 do not apply, and without the clause the proper law would probably be Elbonian. So UCTA would still not help Pascoe against clause 16.

The threshold is sole purpose, tested by the lex fori. Halvard's genuine Arcadian connection and its network-wide use of the form answer the email. So Arcadian law probably governs and the Elbonian Act drops out. Put Pascoe's case first, then say why it probably fails. If it succeeded, the clause would be struck out completely and Elbonian law would govern as the objective proper law.

5Remember

🧠 FOR THE EXAM
  • An express choice falls for evasion only if evasion was the sole purpose (Per Peh Teck Quee); a genuine link and a second reason, such as one form for a whole network, usually save it.
  • If an express choice fails (not bona fide, floating or infected), skip implied choice and go straight to the objective proper law (Per Shanghai Turbo and The Iran Vojdan).
  • A foreign statute giving a money right counts only as part of the proper law, whatever it says about exclusion; the overriding statutes are Singapore's own, and a foreign place of performance comes in only through Foster, Ralli or Lemenda.
  • A split fixes each law at signing for a defined part and is allowed if coherent (Per Libyan Arab Foreign Bank); a floating clause fixes none, and its validity is open: void under the lex fori, valid if the objective proper law allows it.
  • A Singapore statute needs its own reach: the Misrepresentation Act only with a Singapore proper law (Per JIO Minerals); UCTA despite a foreign choice only through s 27(2), and s 27(1) switches off ss 2 to 7 where Singapore law governs only by choice.
  • Fundamental public policy is narrower than domestic policy, so it cannot help where Singapore's own law gives the same result.
